def transform(grid):
    from collections import Counter, deque
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    bg = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
    seen = [[False] * w for _ in range(h)]
    objs = []
    for r in range(h):
        for c in range(w):
            if grid[r][c] == bg or seen[r][c]:
                continue
            color = grid[r][c]
            q = [(r, c)]
            seen[r][c] = True
            cells = []
            for y, x in q:
                cells.append((y, x))
                for dy, dx in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                    ny, nx = y + dy, x + dx
                    if 0 <= ny < h and 0 <= nx < w and not seen[ny][nx] and grid[ny][nx] == color:
                        seen[ny][nx] = True
                        q.append((ny, nx))
            objs.append((color, cells))
    # The target is the object whose bounding box has a complete top and bottom edge.
    target = None
    for color, cells in objs:
        rs = [p[0] for p in cells]
        cs = [p[1] for p in cells]
        r0, r1, c0, c1 = min(rs), max(rs), min(cs), max(cs)
        cellset = set(cells)
        if all((r0, c) in cellset for c in range(c0, c1 + 1)) and all((r1, c) in cellset for c in range(c0, c1 + 1)):
            if target is None or len(cells) > len(target[1]):
                target = (color, cells, (r0, r1, c0, c1))
    color, cells, (r0, r1, c0, c1) = target
    # Marker color comes from small objects of another color.
    candidates = [(len(cs), col) for col, cs in objs if col != color]
    marker = min(candidates)[1]
    return [[color if grid[r][c] == color else marker for c in range(c0, c1 + 1)] for r in range(r0, r1 + 1)]

                y, x = stack.pop()

                for dy, dx in ((1, 0), (-1, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1)):
                    ny, nx = y + dy, x + dx
                    if 0 <= ny < h and 0 <= nx < w and not seen[ny][nx] and grid[ny][nx] == color:
                        seen[ny][nx] = True
                        stack.append((ny, nx))
            objects.append((color, cells))
